nodes.name: List the cohorts
nodes.notes: Reads the plan and state. `collected` on each cohort is what makes the loop resumable.

nodes.name: Listed?
nodes.notes: False usually means stage 02 has not produced a plan yet — nothing to loop over.

nodes.name: Any uncollected?
nodes.notes: False means every cohort is already collected — a re-run of a finished month does nothing, which is the point.

nodes.name: Next cohort
nodes.notes: One cohort per iteration. Convin holds a global per-tenant lock, so concurrency buys nothing — and one row per cohort is what makes a stall visible while it is happening.

nodes.name: 03 · Export cohort
nodes.notes: Fires the Convin export for one cohort and verifies request_params server-side before waiting.

nodes.name: 03 ok?
nodes.notes: crash → retry with backoff. stop → escalate now, amber.

nodes.name: 04 · Collect cohort
nodes.notes: Collects the report email and runs repair_calllog.mjs. A non-zero repair exit is fatal.

nodes.name: 04 ok?
nodes.notes: Same retry policy as 03 — the same cohort is re-exported and re-collected.

nodes.name: Decide retry
nodes.notes: Crash → up to 3 attempts, 5/10/20 minutes apart. Stop → escalate immediately, amber. Never converts a failure into "no calls".

nodes.name: Retry?
nodes.notes: True → back off and re-fire. False → mark failed, escalate, carry on with the rest.

nodes.name: Back off
nodes.notes: 2^(attempt-1) × 5 minutes: 5, 10, 20. Convin jobs take 4-6 minutes when healthy, so a shorter first wait would re-fire into a job that is still running.

nodes.name: Mark the cohort failed
nodes.notes: Writes failed:true into state/<month>.json. A failed cohort must stay visibly failed — never readable downstream as a cohort with no calls. The command is wrapped so the shell always exits 0 and the real code travels in stdout as __EXIT__<code>. Measured on n8n 2.35.7: this node reports exitCode ONLY when the command exits 0 — on any non-zero exit it emits { error } alone, dropping both exitCode and stdout, with the stderr text as the message. That makes an exit 10 (a human must decide) indistinguishable from a crash, and loses the JSON line the contract is built on. onError:continueRegularOutput keeps the workflow running but does not restore the fields.

nodes.name: Escalate
nodes.notes: Amber for a stop, red for a crash. The severity comes from the outcome, not from the fact that we gave up.

nodes.name: Summarise the loop
nodes.notes: monthIncomplete=true means the Orchestrator must skip stages 05-07 rather than build on partial data.
